scenario.name: Kubernetes Official Docs, Falco Security & MITRE — Ephemeral Debug Container (kubectl debug) Shared Process Namespace Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine an armored cash-transport van engineered with zero interior door handles and zero toolboxes so nobody can operate inside it. Using a special roadside-mechanic pass, an intruder bolts a temporary diagnostic side cabin directly onto the armored van shared interior cabin, reads every secret vault note taped beside the driver seat, and leaves a permanent weld scar that forces the bank to retire and replace the entire vehicle. In this scenario (T1609, Kubernetes Official Docs, Falco Security & MITRE, Ephemeral Debug Container , kubectl debug Shared Process Namespace Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: subresource PATCH Against, then process Namespace Targeting, then interactive SPDY/WebSocket pods/attach. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Subresource PATCH Against, then Process Namespace Targeting, then Interactive SPDY/WebSocket pods/attach, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Kubernetes Audit Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Separate pods/ephemeralcontainers RBAC permissions from standard developer roles and require break-glass approval or admission policy checks before allowing ephemeral container attachment in production.

stages.title: Stage 1: Subresource PATCH Against /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<pod>/ephemeralcontainers
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1609 - Container Administration Command)
stages.description: Even though the armored payments van carries no shell or repair tools inside its cabin, the intruder flashes a specialized roadside-debug permit to weld a fully equipped temporary service booth straight onto the live moving vehicle. Even when a production pod uses a hardened distroless image with no shell (/bin/sh removed), an identity with pods/ephemeralcontainers permissions can run kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox --target=app to inject an interactive ephemeral container into the running pod (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with TargetSubresource=pods/ephemeralcontainers, InjectedEphemeralContainer=debugger-8x2lq , image: nicolaka/netshoot, TargetContainerName=payment-app so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '. | select(.objectRef.subresource=="ephemeralcontainers")' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.objectRef.subresource=="ephemeralcontainers"' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1609 during "Subresource PATCH Against /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<pod>/ephemeralcontainers" , Even when a production pod uses a hardened distroless image with no shell , /bin/sh removed, an identity with pods/ephemeralcontainers permissions can run kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox --target=app to inject an interactive ephemeral container into the running pod while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl get pod payment-service-5c8 -n prod -o jsonpath="{.spec.ephemeralContainers}" runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get pod payment-service-5c8 -n prod -o jsonpath="{.spec.ephemeralContainer so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1609 during "Subresource PATCH Against /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<pod>/ephemeralcontainers" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). stages.title: Stage 2: Process Namespace Targeting (--target) & Reading /proc/<pid>/environ Secrets
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.001 - Credentials In Files / ProcFS)
stages.description: Linking the temporary service booth directly into the main driver cabin wall, the intruder reaches straight into the active driver workspace and photocopies every live vault key and database password taped inside memory. Because targetContainerName="payment-app" instructs the container runtime (containerd) to join the ephemeral container to the target container PID namespace, the ephemeral shell can directly read /proc/1/environ and /proc/1/root/app/config (logged in Linux Audit Event 257 with EphemeralContainer=debugger-8x2lq, AccessedProcFsPath=/proc/1/environ & /proc/1/root/, SharedNamespace=Target Container PID Namespace , payment-app so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -f /proc/1/environ -i (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -f /proc/1/environ -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact a so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.001 during "Process Namespace Targeting , --target & Reading /proc/<pid>/environ Secrets" , Because targetContainerName="payment-app" instructs the container runtime , containerd to join the ephemeral container to the target container PID namespace, the ephemeral shell can directly read /proc/1/environ and /proc/1/root/app/config while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl describe pod payment-service-5c8 -n prod runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl describe pod payment-service-5c8 -n prod configuring pod security contexts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1552.001 during "Process Namespace Targeting , --target & Reading /proc/<pid>/environ Secrets" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ tr "\0" "\n" < /proc/1/environ (inside ephemeral container debugger-8x2lq) / ⇠#2 ACK 257) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 kube-apiserver (pods/ephemeralcontainers)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Target App Process (/proc/1/environ)).

keySpecs.value: Deploy Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper policies restricting spec.ephemeralContainers images to signed internal diagnostic images and alert via Falco whenever an ephemeral container reads /proc/*/environ or /proc/*/mem.

stages.title: Stage 3: Interactive SPDY/WebSocket pods/attach Session Audit & Pod Rollout Replacement
stages.subtitle: Collection & Command and Control (T1609 - Container Administration Command)
stages.description: Because the bolted-on diagnostic booth can never be unbolted while the armored van remains on the road, investigators audit the live radio session log and dispatch a clean replacement van while retiring the compromised vehicle completely. Because Kubernetes ephemeral containers cannot be removed from a running Pod once added (spec.ephemeralContainers is append-only), defenders terminate the pods/attach stream and replace the Pod via kubectl rollout restart (logged in Linux Audit Event 101 with AttachSubresource=pods/attach , container=debugger-8x2lq, HttpResponseCode=101 Switching Protocols , SPDY/WebSocket, RemediationAction=Delete & recreate Pod to clear ephemeralContainers so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '. | select(.objectRef.subresource=="attach" and .objectRef.name=="payment-service-5c8")' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.objectRef.subresource=="attach" and .objectRef.name=="payment-service-5c8"' so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1609 during "Interactive SPDY/WebSocket pods/attach Session Audit & Pod Rollout Replacement" , Because Kubernetes ephemeral containers cannot be removed from a running Pod once added , spec while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl delete pod payment-service-5c8 -n prod runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl delete pod payment-service-5c8 -n prod configuring pod security contexts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1609 during "Interactive SPDY/WebSocket pods/attach Session Audit & Pod Rollout Replacement" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ CREATE /api/v1/namespaces/prod/pods/payment-service-5c8/attach?container=debugger-8x2lq / ⇠#3 ACK 101) from Node ③ (#3 kube-apiserver (pods/ephemeralcontainers)) to Node ④ (#4 Ephemeral Debug Container (debugger-*)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Target App Process (/proc/1/environ)).

keySpecs.value: Alert on correlated pods/ephemeralcontainers PATCH followed by pods/attach CREATE in Kubernetes Audit logs, and immediately recycle any production Pod that has an unexpected entry in status.ephemeralContainerStatuses.
